scope: MTADF paper-policy isotonic and global/local logistic methods, decisions and complete-cohort simulations; recovered author-reference isotonic, local logistic and global logistic decision, replay and serial simulation workflows

sources.role: Primary author manuscript: Sections 2.2 and 2.4 define global quadratic and local linear logistic models, independent Cauchy priors, local slope thresholds, bounce guard and isotonic final selection.
Identifies double-sided isotonic regression as the implemented method, provides complete-count trial conduct and operating-characteristic settings, and cites Zang, Lee and Yuan (2014).
Primary mathematical specification: Section 2.1 beta-binomial safety and prior elicitation; Section 2.3 weighted PAVA, unweighted split scores, lowest-dose efficacy ties and adaptive exploration.
Authors' institutional index linking the paper and reference R implementation.

Full primary author reference recovered (20,787 bytes). Separate isotonic, local logistic and global logistic APIs preserve fixed safety calibration and source-specific decisions, final selection and cohort conduct. Local fits use full-grid adjacent windows and source slope gates; global fits use the recovered arm variance-adjusted IRLS coefficient procedure.

Era-matched primary dependency source for patient-expanded predictor scaling, centered intercept prior, variance-adjusted IRLS and convergence. Direct private-fit R reference checks four datasets; exact historical app dependency version is unknown.

implementation_choices: Independent implementation of the paper's isotonic method; dose indices are zero-based.
Pool posterior overdose probabilities with equal PAVA weights and require strict probability below the safety cutoff; stop if no dose is admissible.
Calibrate a common Beta prior from the requested toxicity limit, cutoff, margin and concentration instead of a fixed hidden prior.
Fit efficacy only at observed doses using patient-count PAVA weights; rank candidate splits by unweighted squared error as printed in the paper.
Interpret the apparent y_k/n_k index typo inside the paper's sum over j as the observed rate y_j/n_j.
Safety takes priority over one-level movement. Isotonic final recommendations require observed outcomes at candidate doses; unobserved efficacy remains undefined in that design.
Simulation uses independent binary toxicity and efficacy margins, complete cohort ascertainment, serial trials and bounded work; simulate_mtadf remains isotonic only.
Global/local logistic models use explicit supplied dose coding and bounded serial random-walk Metropolis with warmup-only adaptation, acceptance rates, split R-hat and batch-means MCSE.

Global decisions rank posterior mean efficacy, including model-predicted untried doses at final selection. Local decisions use initial ramp, slope thresholds and the next-window bounce guard, with isotonic final selection.
Logistic safety-only actions precede efficacy fitting; boundary clamping, lowest-dose ties and low-boundary local windows are explicit Python conduct choices.

Explicit author-reference isotonic APIs preserve the recovered R decision and simulator policies; the paper-policy APIs remain unchanged. A tight prior root and a scalar unimodal-fit convention are documented Python numerical choices.

Author local logistic APIs permit an unobserved adjacent neighbor, apply the recovered ce1/ce2 slope gates and use bounded explicit Python MCMC. Replay preserves the source cap-one override, otherwise lagged cap, and author isotonic final selection; exact uint64 outcome/sampler seed pairs support reproducibility.

Author global fitting uses grouped-count QR algebra preserving the expanded Bernoulli first step, patient-replicated prior scaling and variance-adjusted prior updates. A one-observed-dose fit is made exactly flat to prevent rounding-dependent peak selection. Simulation fits after every cohort, moves under the previous safety cap, refreshes safety and selects from the last fit under the fresh cap. Nonconverged fits cannot drive decisions.
limitations: The recovered isotonic, local logistic and global logistic workflows are implemented and numerically checked. Python uses tight prior calibration, a mathematically defined singleton isotonic fit and an exactly flat global fit with one observed dose. Local MCMC exposes convergence diagnostics and differs from native metrop proposals/randomness. Historical dependency versions and live-app settings remain unknown; identical native outputs and random streams are not claimed. Paper-policy APIs retain their documented independent choices.
